decisions.reason: Although technologically close to the core business, its disappearance from observed market communication for two years suggests results likely fell below aspiration, so a boundedly rational firm would reallocate resources to stronger wafer lines.

This carrier wafer remains a highly aligned extension of the firm's handling and packaging capabilities, and management would likely retain it unless niche demand for smaller diameters proves persistently too weak.
As a flagship product tightly linked to the firm's strategic direction in advanced packaging wafers, it would typically be given time and R&D slack to mature before being abandoned.
An off-the-shelf brand built on existing glass and quartz wafers uses established capabilities and broadens commercialization with limited extra risk, so it is likely to stay.

Because glass-based circuit boards are more distant from the firm's narrow established substrate business, any shortfall versus aspirations would prompt problemistic search back toward core products and development projects.
